surface_mechanism_description: Hydrogen radicals are effective in reducing TBTDET at the deposition temperature, leading to the formation of Ta-N through the hydrogen reduction reaction of TBTDET. The hydrogen radicals help in converting the C-H species generated by the reduction reaction into more volatile C-H compounds, preventing by-products from residing on the film surface.
evidence: It is thus reasonable to expect that when the TBTDET molecules adsorbed on the surface of the films are exposed to hydrogen radicals, the alkyl groups in TBTDET would be easily reduced to volatile compounds, and the doubly bonded nitrogen atom would have a higher probability of remaining because the doubly bonded nitrogen atom should be bound more strongly to the tantalum atom than the singly bonded nitrogen atoms. Therefore, Ta-N would be formed with hydrogen radicals via the hydrogen reduction reaction of TBTDET. The hydrogen radicals would help the possible C-H species, which would be generated by the hydrogen reduction reaction of TBTDET, and be converted into more volatile C-H compounds, and may prevent by-products from residing on the film surface.
